decisions.title: Monolithic Architecture Pattern
decisions.decision: Single codebase with Express backend and React frontend in monorepo
decisions.rationale: Replit enforces single container deployment; team size of 1-2 developers for MVP; simplicity over distributed systems; rapid MVP delivery with no network overhead between services

decisions.title: Drizzle ORM
decisions.decision: Type-safe lightweight ORM with pg driver for database access
decisions.rationale: Type-safe query builder with excellent DX; lightweight and Replit-compatible unlike Prisma or TypeORM; supports migration management via drizzle-kit; pg driver with connection pooling (max 10, idleTimeoutMillis 30000, connectionTimeoutMillis 2000)

decisions.title: JWT Authentication
decisions.decision: Stateless JWT authentication with refresh token rotation
decisions.rationale: Stateless scaling with no session store dependency; Constitution mandated JWT with 15-minute access tokens and 7-day refresh tokens; refresh tokens stored in database with token_hash, expires_at, revoked_at; rotation invalidates old token and issues new pair on refresh

decisions.title: Query-Level Multi-Tenancy
decisions.decision: Enforce multi-tenancy through explicit organizationId filters on all queries
decisions.rationale: Explicit control and clear audit trail with no magic behavior; easier debugging than middleware injection; all tenant queries must include organization_id filter; helper function withOrgFilter(orgId, query) mitigates manual filtering overhead

decisions.title: Stream-Based File Processing
decisions.decision: Stream-based CSV/Excel/JSON parsing with strict validation and size limits
decisions.rationale: Memory-efficient processing prevents DoS and OOM crashes; supports 50MB CSV requirement; MIME type whitelist (text/csv, xlsx, application/json) with magic number detection; streaming parsers (csv-parser, xlsx-stream, JSONStream) for large files; temporary storage in /tmp/uploads with crypto.randomBytes filenames

decisions.title: In-Memory Job Queue
decisions.decision: In-memory batch processing queue for MVP using express-rate-limit pattern; async job queue with status tracking
decisions.rationale: Redis forbidden due to port conflicts on Replit; single-server in-memory rate limiting and job processing acceptable for MVP with 20 concurrent users; distributed job queue deferred to post-MVP when multi-instance scaling required

decisions.title: Replit Deployment
decisions.decision: Single container deployment on Replit with production binding to 0.0.0.0:5000
decisions.rationale: Replit enforces single container with ephemeral filesystem and port 5000; explicit IPv4 binding prevents localhost IPv6/IPv4 mismatch causing ECONNREFUSED; development backend on 127.0.0.1:3001, production on 0.0.0.0:5000; Vite dev server on 0.0.0.0:5000 with proxy to http://127.0.0.1:3001; Constitution Section C mandate

decisions.title: Cryptographic Randomness
decisions.decision: Use crypto.randomBytes() for all security-sensitive random value generation including tokens, session IDs, filenames, and invitation codes
decisions.rationale: Math.random() provides only ~48-bit entropy and is predictable; crypto.randomBytes provides 128-256 bit cryptographic entropy; prevents session hijacking, token forgery, and file enumeration attacks; Constitution Section C mandate; 16 bytes for session IDs and filenames, 32 bytes for CSRF and password reset tokens

decisions.title: PII De-identification
decisions.decision: Hybrid approach combining regex patterns for structured data and NLP Named Entity Recognition via compromise library for names and addresses
decisions.rationale: Core product feature requiring >95% detection accuracy; regex alone misses context-dependent PII while NER alone may miss structured data like SSNs and credit cards; three replacement strategies supported: mask (NAME), token ([NAME_hex]), and synthetic (fake replacement); manual review queue for low-confidence matches; target >95% recall and >90% precision
